title: Customer briefing: model-fallback routing event and interim guidance
content:
Executive summary:

This is a customer-facing draft for a status page update and short post-incident communication describing the model-fallback routing event that affected a subset of inference requests on 2026-03-29. We intend to publish a concise status update now and follow up with a more detailed postmortem.

What happened (short):
- Between 2026-03-29T10:18:00Z and 2026-03-29T11:07:00Z, a routing policy regression caused a proportion of production requests to be routed to a lower-capacity compatibility pool. That pool hosted a quantized variant of our primary model and had degraded KV-cache hit rates; requests served from that pool experienced elevated latency and a small spike in 5xx stream closures.
- Impact: approximately 4.7% of active generation requests across multiple hosted regions. Most customer API calls succeeded with higher latency; about 0.3% experienced failures returned to clients (stream early terminations / 503s).

Immediate status page copy (short update for publication):
- Title: Partial routing disruption affecting a subset of generation requests
- Summary: We experienced a routing regression that led to some requests being served from a lower-capacity model pool. Customers may have seen increased latency or intermittent failed streams for a small fraction of requests. Our engineers applied configuration mitigations and traffic has been routed back to standard pools. We continue to monitor.
- Affected time window: 2026-03-29 10:18–11:07 UTC
- Current status: mitigated; monitoring
- Next update: detailed post-incident summary in 48–72 hours or sooner if new information arises

Customer-facing technical summary / postmortem (concise):
Root cause (high level):
- A change to the smart-routing weight calculation (deployed as part of a traffic-shaping tuning PR) introduced a condition where capacity signals from the autoscaler were considered stale for up to 4 minutes when cluster-level telemetry lagged. During a short telemetry blackout, the routing layer preferred a fallback compatibility pool that was intended only for overflow. That pool was running a quantized model variant with different KV cache sizing and lower throughput per GPU.
- Two compounding factors increased customer impact: (1) the compatibility pool had higher KV cache miss rates for long-chat sessions, resulting in higher per-token latency, and (2) our legacy stream-retry logic closed some long-running streams rather than transparently reconnecting under degraded throughput.

Customer impact (details):
- Scope: multi-region hosted API (US-West, EU-Central); not observed in private deployments with pinned models.
- Symptom types observed by customers: increased p95/p99 latency for generation; occasional stream early-termination errors (clients received partial payloads); no data leakage or content corruption.
- Percentages: ~4.7% of generation requests routed to fallback pool; ~0.3% of all generation requests returned a terminal error; token-level cost impact varied by customer depending on session lengths.

What we did (mitigation timeline, concise):
- 10:18 UTC — Monitoring alert triggered (elevated p95 latency and stream closes).
- 10:22 UTC — On-call engineer enabled a temporary routing hold to freeze new decisions to fallback pool.
- 10:35 UTC — Autoscaler telemetry ingestion was force-restarted to clear the lagging metrics pipeline.
- 10:47 UTC — Traffic steering rule updated to prefer primary pools; rollback of the traffic-shaping PR staged.
- 11:07 UTC — Routing returned to normal; error rates and latency trended back to baseline by 11:25 UTC.

Interim customer recommendations (what customers can do right now):
- For customers using our hosted API and seeing failures: implement idempotent request retries with exponential backoff (recommended base backoff 150ms, multiplier 2, max retries 3).
- For customers concerned about quality variability during unusual routing events: pin to a particular model variant via the model parameter (e.g., model=redwood-1.1-standard) to avoid automatic fallback routing until the postmortem is complete. Note: pinning affects availability during capacity-constrained windows but preserves model quality and latency characteristics.
- For streaming consumers: incorporate client-side reconnection logic to resume interrupted streams and to request a short-range token window if partial output was received. Our SDK teams will publish updated examples for graceful streaming reconnection.

Planned follow-ups and remediation (next 72 hours / engineering actions):
- Full rollback of the routing weight-change commit and a test-suite addition to prevent stale-telemetry acceptance in the weight calc (target: 48 hours).
- Add a short-circuit in the routing decision path to avoid selecting lower-quality pools when KV cache miss rate for a session exceeds a threshold (target: 1 week for rollout + verification).
- Improve stream-resume behavior so that long-running streams degrade gracefully instead of returning terminal 5xx on transient throughput drops (target: 2 weeks).
- Postmortem will include timeline, root-cause analysis artifacts, and lessons learned; we will publish a customer-facing summary within 72 hours.

Compensation / credits:
- We recognize disruption for a subset of requests. Our standard approach is to evaluate incidents with customer impact for service credits on a case-by-case basis once the postmortem is finalized. If you experienced measurable impact beyond brief latency increases (e.g., repeated failed transactions, operational cost increases), please open a support ticket referencing JIRA-RI-4217 and include example request IDs/timestamps.

Contact and escalation path:
- Primary customer contact: customer-success@redwood.inference (for account-level follow-up and credits).
- Technical liaison for high-severity cases: Jordan Patel (jordan.patel@redwood.inference). Include request IDs and a short description of observed symptoms for faster triage.

Notes to internal readers (do not publish):
- Verify telemetry timeline with infra team before publishing the final postmortem; current telemetry blackout window edges are still under investigation (possible cron job lockup in metrics pipeline).
- Coordinate final credit decisions with finance and legal — incident meets threshold for review but credit amount depends on long-term client exposure.

Draft status and approvals required:
- This document is a draft intended for initial status page posting and a customer-facing postmortem skeleton. Requires review from eng-serving-runtime (Liam O'Connor), infra (Asha Kapoor) and legal for wording on credits.

Attachments / example text snippets for status page UI (short copy):
- Short banner: "Partial routing disruption mitigated — some generation requests saw increased latency or intermittent failures. We have restored normal routing and are investigating."
- Longer line for incident details page: "A routing configuration regression briefly directed a small subset of requests to a lower-capacity model pool; mitigation steps have restored normal traffic and we will publish a detailed postmortem soon."

Prepared by: Jordan Patel for Customer Success.
